title: docs: every `json` fence under content/docs parses; annotated ones are `jsonc` (objectui#10088)
body:
Fixes #10088

Clause-②: no — published docs examples and a repo gate; no accept set or public contract surface moves

Every `json`-tagged fence under `content/docs` now survives `JSON.parse`. A fence that annotates JSON with comments is tagged `jsonc`, and it parses under that dialect too. No gate script and no workflow changed. Whether a gate should *block* on this is raised as its own decision in the report, not landed here, as the card's acceptance asks.

## The convention (named, not invented)

It is the contract `scripts/check-skill-examples.mjs` already states in `parseJsonFence` for the skills tree (objectui#7474 brought that corpus to "parses under its own tag"):

- **`json`** — `JSON.parse` and nothing else. It is what a reader copies into a `.json` metadata file.
- **`jsonc`** — comments (and trailing commas) removed, then **one** JSON document. The tag tells the reader that the fence carries annotation, which is how a deliberate note is told apart from a mistake. A `json` fence that does not parse is a mistake.
- No JSON dialect admits a raw newline inside a string, several documents in one fence, or `...`. Those shapes become one-line strings, one fence per document, and removed elisions.
- Counter-examples still parse. In every "bad" example on these pages the fault is semantic (an expensive or opaque expression, an unknown prop), not syntactic, so the example should parse.

## Per fence (lines at the base commit `733fd5ac65`)

| # | page:line | before-shape | fix kind | tag after |
|--:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `guide/deployment.md:277` | `//` file-name caption (`railway.json (excerpt)`) | retag; the caption is the page's only statement of the file name | `jsonc` |
| 2 | `guide/expressions.md:223` | inline `//` member note (`'item' is scoped data`) | retag | `jsonc` |
| 3 | `guide/expressions.md:337` | raw newlines inside a `${…}` string | expression moved onto one line | `json` |
| 4 | `guide/expressions.md:351` | raw newlines inside a `${…}` string | one line | `json` |
| 5 | `guide/expressions.md:364` | raw newlines inside a `${…}` string | one line | `json` |
| 6 | `guide/expressions.md:380` | raw newlines inside a `${…}` string | one line | `json` |
| 7 | `guide/expressions.md:529` | `// ❌ Bad` label, one document, then a dangling `// ✅ Good` label for the tsx block below | each label becomes the line above its block | `json` |
| 8 | `guide/expressions.md:673` | bad/good pair: two documents plus `//` labels | split into one fence per document, labels above | `json` ×2 |
| 9 | `guide/expressions.md:687` | bad/good pair | split | `json` ×2 |
| 10 | `guide/expressions.md:701` | bad/good pair | split | `json` ×2 |
| 11 | `guide/layout.md:237` | `//` member comment + `[...]` | comment dropped (the page's Schema API block states `maxWidth`), `[...]` changed to `[]` | `json` |
| 12 | `guide/layout.md:507` | three `[...]` | `[]` | `json` |
| 13 | `guide/layout.md:660` | two `//` comments + `[...]` | comments dropped (Schema API block states the `padding` default), `[]` | `json` |
| 14 | `guide/layout.md:743` | `//` comment + `[...]` | comment dropped (the heading says "for Forms"), `[]` | `json` |
| 15 | `guide/schema-rendering.md:273` | raw newlines inside a `${…}` string | one line | `json` |
| 16 | `plugins/index.md:355` | trailing `//` standing for the elided keys ("on the node itself") | retag; the comment carries the teaching | `jsonc` |
| 17 | `utilities/runner.mdx:213` | `package.json` member excerpt (an object body) | wrapped in braces | `json` |
| 18 | `utilities/runner.mdx:246` | trailing `//` for elided keys ("not a `props` envelope") | retag | `jsonc` |
| 19 | `utilities/runner.mdx:292` | three `"..."` elision members | removed | `json` |
| 20 | `utilities/runner.mdx:496` | `//` file-name caption | retag | `jsonc` |
| 21 | `utilities/vscode-extension.mdx:187` | `// ❌ Error: Unknown property`, the counter-example's point | retag | `jsonc` |
| + | `guide/troubleshooting.md:369` | a **`jsonc`** fence holding three documents, rejected by both `parseJsonFence(…, 'jsonc')` and `jsonc-parser` | split, labels above | `json` ×3 |

The last row is outside the `json` population. It is in the claim's file surface and is the same defect class: its tag's grammar rejects its body. It gets the same mechanical split as rows 8–10, so the convention holds for the whole of `content/docs` with no exception.

## The premise, re-measured

The instrument walks `git ls-files content/docs` (`.md`/`.mdx`), pairs fences with the repo's `scripts/markdown-fence-scan.mjs`, and runs strict `JSON.parse` on every fence whose language is exactly `json`. Controls run in the same command: `{"a":1,}` is REJECTED and `{"a":1}` is ACCEPTED.

- base `733fd5ac65`: 184 files, **203** `json` fences, **21** failing. The PM probe's 209 / 24 also counted the six `jsonc` fences, three of which fail a strict parse. `fields/location.mdx` and `guide/record-edit-modes.md` are correctly tagged `jsonc` and parse under it (both instruments). `guide/troubleshooting.md` is the `+` row above.
- final head: **203** `json` fences, **0** failing; **11** `jsonc` fences, **0** failing under `parseJsonFence(…, 'jsonc')` and under `jsonc-parser` (with the error list read). Controls: a comment is ACCEPTED, while `[...]` and two documents are REJECTED by both.

## Why the one existing gate was not tightened

The gate that reads these fences is `scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs`, which is report-only. It normalises away **five** shapes the 21 used, not two: comments, raw newlines, elisions, the object-body retry, and several top-level documents. It treats `json` and `jsonc` alike. At the base commit it printed `231 json/jsonc fence(s), 231 parsed, 0 UNPARSED (1 parsed as an object body)`. I left it alone for two reasons:

1. **Its tolerances are there on purpose.** Its header says so: it judges `${…}` carriage inside annotated fences, and "reaches 0 unparsed over the whole tree, which takes four tolerances beyond `JSON.parse`". The card says the same thing: "Not a defect in that gate — it was built for a different question".
2. **Tightening it would change how strong a gate is, and the card keeps that decision for a human.** `check-doc-expression-carriage.test.ts` › "has no blind spot on the corpus it ships against" asserts `census.unparsed` is empty on the real tree. That test runs on every pull request that touches `content/docs`: `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --changed -` lists all eight pages this PR touches, so the test job in `ci.yml` runs everything. Parsing `json` strictly would therefore make a non-JSON `json` fence block the merge. The card's acceptance covers exactly this: "if the answer is 「it should」, that is raised as its own decision rather than landed inside this card". The report raises it.

After the change, the census reads the same content. It printed `417 node(s) … 68 ${…} site(s) … 65 of them carried` before and after, and the three findings are identical apart from line numbers. The fence count went from 231 to 236 (json 221 → 221, jsonc 10 → 15), and nothing is parsed as an object body any more.

## The one test that changed, and a mutation that shows it can fail

`packages/types/src/__tests__/page-actions-refusal-7926.test.ts` pinned `guide/layout.md`'s four unparseable `json` fences (the `[...]` elisions) as its blind spot, by exact count. That count is now zero. So the census judges those four `page` nodes (no `actions`, content under `children`) instead of skipping them. An unparseable `json` fence on that page was already red before, as 5 against the pinned 4, so the pin is no stronger or weaker than it was.

Mutation, run with objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` from the committed head `f957ff9252`: anchor `"children": []` hit ×1 and was replaced by `"children": [...]` (`anchor 1 → 0`, blob `570a150066be → c26fd61cea62`). The pin then failed with `AssertionError: expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []`, naming `content/docs/guide/layout.md:660` (`Tests 1 failed | 10 passed`). Restored with `blob == HEAD (570a150066be) and git diff HEAD is empty`.

## Local verification (final head `f1edd2dd3d`, after merging `origin/main` `29c76e573c`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over the 25 tests `scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs` names as readers of the touched pages, plus 5 grep-found neighbours: `Test Files 30 passed (30)`, `Tests 1173 passed (1173)`, run under the verify lock.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`: exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the changed test (1 hit).
- `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:doc-example-readers`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`) and `docs:check-links`: all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, with an empty-frontmatter changeset for the one `src/` test file. `check-changeset-no-major`: exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs`: exit 0, `236 … 236 parsed, 0 UNPARSED`, `Blind spot: none`.
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:doc-snippets`, `check:doc-examples`.** Reason: `THE GATE COULD NOT RUN`, because 34 packages are unbuilt in this worktree. The narrowing was measured instead: across the 8 touched pages, `scanFences` from `check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` returns the same 52 ts/tsx/typescript blocks at the base and at the head. Body, quote depth and fragment-marker binding are all unchanged (28 are fragment-declared). A control confirms that a detached marker reads as changed. CI runs both gates in full.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- `packages/vscode-extension/README.md:125` is a `json` fence with `//` comments (VS Code settings are JSONC). It sits on the carriage surface, outside `content/docs`, and is the only json/jsonc fence there that fails under its own tag. Carrier: none.
- `guide/layout.md` teaches `maxWidth` and `padding` on a `page` node. A source grep of `renderers/layout/page.tsx` finds no `schema.maxWidth` or `schema.padding` read, but AGENTS.md says a grep zero cannot answer "no renderer reads this key", so this is **unmeasured**, not asserted. Carrier: none.
- `guide/schema-rendering.md`'s Memoization claim is the card's unmeasured neighbour. It is still unmeasured: this PR did not take a reading in either direction.
- The dispatch assumed that docs-only PRs skip the CI test shards. For `content/docs`, the test job's decision step reads `markdown-test-inputs.mjs` and runs everything.
